Notebook.Title: Load Test: Five Ways to Sum a Million Requests

Section.Title: Welcome
Section.Paragraph: Both cells share Scope="load-test". The entity count here is 100,000 rather than the million a standalone benchmark binary would use — enough to see the strategies separate on the clock without making a live in-browser recompile-and-run sluggish.

Section.Title: Scene 1: Five Ways to Sum the Same Query
Section.Paragraph: Same data, five access patterns: a plain foreach, ForSlice (a delegate over contiguous component slices), a hand-rolled SIMD reduction via CommunityToolkit.HighPerformance's Cast, ForSliceOnParallel, and ParallelSystemBase<T> (a structured base class for the same idea). Results land in Results.Items, a plain static list any type in this scope can read — that's the "store cross-cell state on a type, not a stray local" pattern in practice.

Section.Title: Bonus Round: a Worker Pool With a Connection Per Thread
Section.Paragraph: Context<T> is thread-static — WorkerPoolRunner sets a distinct IConnectionPool on each of its worker threads once, and every job that thread ever runs can reach it via Context.Get<IConnectionPool>() with no parameter passing. The leaderboard at the end reads Results.Items, populated by Scene 1's systems above.
